name: Capitalism
definition: An economic system based on the private ownership of the means of production and their operation for profit.
core_tenets: Private property rights and freedom of enterprise
Price discovery determined by supply and demand without mandatory central planning
advantages: High economic efficiency, rapid innovation, consumer sovereignty, dynamic capital allocation
critiques: Tendency toward wealth inequality, environmental externalities, business cycle volatility, underprovision of public goods
description: The predominant global economic model characterized by decentralized market mechanisms, private asset stewardship, and competitive pricing incentives.

name: Socialism
definition: An economic and political system characterized by social ownership of the means of production, cooperative management of the economy, and distribution based on human need rather than private profit.
core_tenets: Social or collective ownership of key productive assets (state, cooperative, or municipal)
Production oriented directly towards use value and societal welfare rather than capital accumulation
Robust public provision of healthcare, education, housing, and social security
Reduction or elimination of economic class disparities
advantages: Reduced income disparity, universal access to basic necessities, collective worker empowerment, prioritization of public welfare
critiques: Risk of bureaucratic inefficiencies, potential reduction in entrepreneurial risk incentives, misallocation in rigid central planning
description: A socio-economic philosophy advocating that the resources, tools, and infrastructure of a society should belong to the community as a whole to foster equity and social justice.

name: Mixed Economy
definition: An economic system blending elements of private capitalism with state intervention, regulation, and social welfare provision.
core_tenets: Coexistence of private enterprise and public sector institutions
Market forces govern consumer goods, while government provides public infrastructure, education, defense, and healthcare
Fiscal and monetary policy utilized by the state to moderate economic recessions and inflation
Regulatory protections for labor, consumers, and the environment
description: The most widely implemented economic model in the modern world, striving to harness market efficiency while preventing market failures through targeted governmental stewardship.

name: Mercantilism
definition: An economic policy designed to maximize the exports and minimize the imports for an economy, accumulating monetary reserves through a positive balance of trade, particularly of bullion (gold and silver).
core_tenets: Belief that global wealth is zero-sum, requiring fierce interstate rivalry for trade dominance
High protective tariffs on imported manufactured goods to defend domestic industries
Acquisition of foreign colonial territories as sources of raw materials and exclusive export markets
State-granted monopolies on colonial maritime trade (e.g., British East India Company, Dutch VOC)
description: The prevailing economic orthodoxy of early modern Europe that stimulated colonial expansion and naval militarism, before being superseded by classical free-market economics.
